findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add 'run `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` to ensure the criteria guide contains the T2 section before the guard sweep' as an explicit step in Testing/Approach, so AC5's 'exactly one match' is achievable on the migrated tree.
evidence: Search for '## T2' in docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md: no matches
Search for 'success criteria for a trial' in docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md: no matches
The guide is generated via 'python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide'
plan_review_T2.md confirmed contains 'stated success criteria for a trial' — once the guide is regenerated, it will appear there
The plan's Scope section, Approach section, Testing section, and AC list all omit any mention of running regenerate-criteria-guide
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md — GENERATED from the criteria registry, so it echoes T2's excluded prompt verbatim; the epic's amended AC5 pins it at exactly one match.' However, the current guide file does not contain a T2 section at all (confirmed: no '## T2' heading, no 'success criteria for a trial' phrase). This means the 'exactly one match' claim in AC5 is only true AFTER the guide is regenerated. The plan never explicitly lists guide regeneration as a required step, leaving this AC silently dependent on a prerequisite that is not named in Testing or the edit set.
findings.location: Scope section — 'docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md — GENERATED from the criteria registry…the epic's amended AC5 pins it at exactly one match.' and AC5: 'A full-repo sweep confirms no live-source SC vocabulary remains outside the allowlist.'
scenarios: The guard script runs on the current tree before guide regeneration: it finds zero SC matches in the guide (not one), so the AC5 'exactly one match' assertion fails.
The guard is written to expect one match in the guide and is run in CI on the pre-regeneration tree, causing a false-positive CI failure.
An implementer regenerates the guide as common sense, but without this being in the plan the step can be skipped, leaving the guard to see zero matches.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Testing section: 'Run `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` before the guard sweep to ensure docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md contains the T2 section (which carries the carve-out phrase); AC5's single-match assertion is only checkable on the regenerated guide.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact CI integration point for the guard script — either `make lint` (Makefile recipe) or a standalone `_build-and-test.yml` step — and state the positive rationale for that choice (e.g. standalone step to avoid lengthening pre-commit, with a `make check-sc-vocab` alias for local runs).
evidence: Approach: 'The guard matches the exact phrase case-insensitively... Scoping the bare-token rule by PATH...'
AC1: 'scripts/ carries a guard script wired into an existing CI gate'
Makefile lint recipe: ruff check, ruff format --check, check_dco_identity.py, zizmor, actionlint — no precedent for a broad repo file-scan here
_build-and-test.yml: check_verify_gate_parity.py, check_server_manifest.py run as standalone steps — the established pattern for this type of guard
ABSENCE: no rationale in the plan for which integration point is chosen
findings.finding: The plan says the guard is 'wired into the existing lint/CI gates' but does not specify whether this means (a) added to the `make lint` recipe in the Makefile or (b) added as a standalone step in `_build-and-test.yml`, and provides no positive rationale for that choice. The codebase uses both patterns — `make lint` for ruff/zizmor/actionlint/check_dco_identity, and `_build-and-test.yml` standalone steps for check_verify_gate_parity.py, check_server_manifest.py, and the criteria-routing parity gate. A broad file-scan guard placed in `make lint` lengthens every pre-commit invocation; a standalone CI step without a `make` alias is not locally runnable via the standard developer workflow. The implementer has no specification to follow and could choose either, producing an integration that is inconsistent with expectations.
findings.location: Approach section / AC1 ('wired into an existing CI gate')
scenarios: Implementer adds the guard to make lint, slowing every pre-commit run by a full repo file scan; operator expectation was a CI-only step.
Implementer adds it only as a standalone CI step with no make target, making it unrunnable locally with the standard 'make lint' workflow.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'The guard is wired as a standalone step in `_build-and-test.yml` (consistent with `check_verify_gate_parity.py` and `check_server_manifest.py`), not under `make lint`, to avoid adding a full-repo file scan to the pre-commit hot path. A `python scripts/check_sc_vocab.py` invocation in the CI step makes it locally reproducible without a dedicated `make` target.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the external data-file allowlist is justified over an inline Python constant (matching the pattern in all 6+ sibling guard scripts); if the list is static and bounded as specified, inline it to avoid introducing a new config-surface artifact.
evidence: scripts/check_dco_identity.py uses inline EXCLUDED_PREFIXES tuple and _PATTERN constant — no external data file
scripts/check_build_env_locked.py uses inline BASE_ALLOWLIST = {"pip", "setuptools", "wheel"} — no external data file
scripts/check_docs_index.py uses inline constants — no external data file

The allowlist in the plan's Scope section is bounded (~15 entries): 2 Jira fixtures, docs/archive/, docs/experiments/, 3 historical-citation sites, 4 O-RAN-SC sites, editor.js, 4 permanent vocabulary carve-outs, 2 test files — all statically known and easily inlined
An inline constant is equally 'reviewable as a diff' (changes appear in the script's diff) and matches the established codebase pattern
findings.finding: The plan proposes 'The allowlist is a data file, not inline regex' — but all 6+ existing sibling guard scripts (check_dco_identity.py, check_build_env_locked.py, check_docs_index.py, check_dco_identity.py, etc.) use inline Python constants for their exemption lists (e.g. EXCLUDED_PREFIXES, BASE_ALLOWLIST). An external data-file allowlist introduces a new config-surface pattern for a bounded, static set (~15 enumerated entries) with no forcing function: the plan's own 'reviewable as a diff' rationale applies equally to an inline constant in the script itself.
findings.location: Approach section — 'The allowlist is a data file, not inline regex, so an exemption is reviewable as a diff.'
scenarios: A new contributor adding an exemption must find and edit an external data file rather than the script itself, adding indirection not present in sibling guards
The data file becomes a second artifact to maintain, version, and reference from tests — increasing surface area without benefit over an inline constant
findings.suggested_fix: Use an inline Python constant (e.g. `_ALLOWLIST: frozenset[str] = frozenset({...})`) in the guard script, matching the pattern of check_dco_identity.py's EXCLUDED_PREFIXES and check_build_env_locked.py's BASE_ALLOWLIST. The plan's 'reviewable as a diff' goal is equally served by a constant in the script file.
